title: Introduction and learning outcomes
groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture through the histopathology practicals and outlines the questions it will address.

title: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how research into cancer-causing viruses established that transformation can originate in altered normal cellular genes.

title: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how laboratory assays establish whether a gene or mutation gives cells transformed properties.

title: Functional effects and classification of cancer mutations
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects, using cell-cycle regulation and mutation dominance to demonstrate the distinctions and their limitations.

title: Forms of genetic instability and defects in DNA repair
groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish sequence from chromosomal instability and explain how defective DNA repair produces these phenotypes.

title: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how errors in transmitting the genome to daughter cells generate genetic instability and consequential changes in cancer cells.

title: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing and order of mutation acquisition shape the progression from normal colorectal epithelium to metastatic cancer.

title: Hereditary cancer predisposition and the role of inherited mutations
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how inherited tumor-suppressor defects predispose to cancer, with BRCA2 restoration illustrating why the initiating defect need not remain necessary for malignancy.

title: Further reading, questions, and next lecture
groupedBecause: This closing concludes the learning outcomes and offers questions, recommended reading, and a preview of the next lecture.
